extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for seeking reconsideration, redetermination, reinstatement, and recalculation of Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) before the USPTO, including the interim safe-harbor recalculation process and limits on third-party submissions and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and contents of request for reconsideration (§1.705(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration of the patent term adjustment indicated on the patent must be by way of an application for patent term adjustment filed no later than two months from the date the patent was granted (extendable under §1.136(a)). An application must be accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.18(e) and a statement of the facts involved specifying: (i) the correct patent term adjustment and the basis or bases under §1.702 for the adjustment; (ii) the relevant dates as specified in §§1.703(a) through (e) for which an adjustment is sought and the adjustment as specified in §1.703(f) to which the patent is entitled; (iii) whether the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer and any expiration date specified in the terminal disclaimer; and (iv) either any circumstances during prosecution constituting a failure to engage in reasonable efforts as set forth in §1.704 or that there were no such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-month period may be extended under §1.136(a) (up to five additional months per MPEP discussion). The statement of facts must be specific (dates, bases under §1.702). If the request is not timely filed, the Office will not grant recalculation. If the request for reconsideration is based solely on the Office's failure to recognize a safe harbor statement (pre-July 17, 2023 filings), a special form (PTO/SB/134) may be used (see interim procedure) and the usual fee may be waived in that limited situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office redetermination process and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will conduct a manual redetermination of PTA in response to a request for reconsideration. A redetermination may: (1) result in the amount requested by applicant; (2) result in no change; or (3) result in a different amount (higher or lower).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If redetermination matches applicant's request, Office issues decision granting reconsideration and a certificate of correction indicating revised PTA. If redetermination matches the patent and no additional info is needed, Office issues decision denying reconsideration (Director's decision under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)). If redetermination results in a different amount, Office issues a redetermination explaining how it arrived at the different amount (this is not the Director's final decision). Applicant then has two months from the date of that redetermination to file a renewed request addressing the issues in the redetermination (no additional fee required). The two-month renewal period is extendable under §1.136(a). If the Office issues a requirement for information, applicant has two months to file a renewed request supplying the information (also extendable under §1.136(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requests for PTA reduced for late replies (§1.705(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reinstatement of all or part of the period of adjustment reduced pursuant to §1.704(b) for failing to reply within three months must be filed prior to the issuance of the patent and must be accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.18(f) and a showing to the satisfaction of the Director that, in spite of all due care, the applicant was unable to reply within three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not consider or act on a request for reinstatement filed after the patent issues; a reinstatement request cannot be made as part of a post-issuance reconsideration under §1.705(b). The Office will not grant more than three additional months for each reply beyond three months. Applicants seeking reinstatement should file promptly and at least one day prior to issuance. The Office will decide on the request after grant and may issue a certificate of correction to revise PTA if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘In spite of all due care’ standard for reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing required for reinstatement under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3)(C) is that 'in spite of all due care' the applicant was unable to respond within the three-month period. This invokes a higher degree of care than ordinary due care and the 'reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution' standard of 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard is analogous to the due care of a reasonably prudent person but higher than the 'unavoidable delay' standard (35 U.S.C. 133). MPEP gives positive examples that may establish the showing (e.g., insufficient time to obtain test data for an affidavit/declaration; natural disaster; testing necessarily took longer than three months; illness or death of a sole practitioner of record). It also lists negative examples (e.g., preoccupation with other matters, illness of a practitioner who has colleagues available, delays from communications between applicant and representative, vacation/non-attention, filing by first-class mail on or near the last day instead of e-filing or Priority Mail Express®, clerical docketing failures). Reinstated PTA is limited to the period that the showing establishes applicant acted with all due care but was unable to reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of three-month reply period (application of 35 U.S.C. 21(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 21(b) apply to the determination of the three-month period for reply: if the last day of the three-month period falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday within the District of Columbia, action may be taken or fee paid on the next succeeding secular or business day without loss of any PTA under §1.704(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the three-month deadline falls on a Saturday and the reply is received by the Office on the following Monday (not a federal holiday), the reply is treated as timely and no PTA reduction is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim procedure for recalculation when Office fails to recognize safe harbor statements (pre-July 17, 2023)
rubrics_metrics.description: For safe harbor statements under §1.704(d) filed before July 17, 2023, the Office created an interim procedure allowing a patentee to request recalculation of PTA where the sole reason for contesting the PTA determination is the Office's failure to recognize a timely filed safe harbor statement accompanying an IDS. The interim procedure permits submission of Form PTO/SB/134 in lieu of the normal request and fee under §1.705(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/SB/134 must be filed within the time period of §1.705(b) and the Office will not grant untimely recalculation requests. The interim procedure waives the fee under §1.705(b)(1) as set forth in §1.18(e) for this narrow ground only, but does not waive extension fees (§1.136) or entitle a patentee to refunds for prior §1.705 filings except where paid by mistake or in excess. The Office of Petitions will manually review the request, and patentee is given one opportunity to respond to the recalculation within two months (no extensions). If patentee's response seeks changes unrelated to the safe harbor issue, patentee must comply with §1.705(b)(1) and (2) (i.e., pay fee and provide full statement). If patentee fails to respond and recalculation differs from printed patent, the Office will sua sponte issue a certificate of correction reflecting the recalculated PTA. The interim procedure is not applicable to safe harbor statements filed on or after July 17, 2023 (the Office updated its PTA program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of combined filings (PTO/SB/134 and §1.705 request)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patentee files both Form PTO/SB/134 and a request under §1.705(b) prior to the Office's recalculation, the Office will treat both papers together as a request for reconsideration under §1.705(b) and require the fee set forth in §1.18(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees should file only the appropriate paper for their ground of contest (solely safe harbor recognition -> PTO/SB/134 when applicable; other issues or mixed issues -> full §1.705(b) request with fee) to avoid unexpected fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions not considered (§1.705(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: No submission or petition on behalf of a third party concerning patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) will be considered by the Office; any such submission or petition will be returned or otherwise disposed of at the Office's convenience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implements 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)(B) for patents granted on or after January 14, 2013 (and analogous pre-2013 provision for earlier patents). Third parties should not expect the Office to act on PTA challenges submitted on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal remedy and exclusivity of civil action (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Only if the Office issues a decision denying patentee’s request for reconsideration may patentee appeal such decision by filing a civil complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days of the date of the decision on the request for reconsideration (under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIA Technical Corrections Act clarified that a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(4) is the exclusive remedy for an applicant dissatisfied with the Director’s decision on a request for reconsideration under 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(3). Thus, applicants must first request reconsideration under §1.705(b); only after receiving a denial may they bring the civil action. For patents issued prior to January 14, 2013, earlier versions of the statute applied (historical differences and tolling issues are discussed in MPEP).
